5: We wait to start Arvit (the evening prayer) on the entry of Shavuot in order that the days of counting (of the Omer) be complete.

(1) And we read in the first (Torah scroll) from "In the third month."  Regarding what we are accustomed to do in these lands (which is) to read the first verse (of the Torah portion) and then begin (reciting) "Akdamut milin," etc.  There is reason to be greatly surprised how we are permitted to interrupt the reading (of the Torah portion) because even to speak words of Torah is forbidden as is written in section 146 and all the (bases  for) permission that are referenced there do not (apply) here, all the more so that this praise (i.e. the text of Akdamut) is not relevant to the Torah portion at all, (therefore) how can we interrupt?  And I heard ?recently? that many eminent rabbis have instructed to sing Akdamut before the Kohen starts the blessing on the Torah reading, and thus is appropriate to practice in all congregations.  So too with Yetziv Pitgam which is recited on the second day after the first verse of the Haftarah, it is appropriate to practice thusly, except that the (laws of reciting the) Haftarah is not as strict as (with) reading the Torah.
